0.long_answer: Bronchopulmonary dysplasia (BPD) is a chronic lung disease most commonly seen in premature infants, particularly those born before 37 weeks’ gestation who require prolonged mechanical ventilation due to respiratory distress. The disease develops as these infants' immature lungs are exposed to oxygen therapy and mechanical ventilation, which can cause injury leading to inflammation and abnormal repair processes. This results in disrupted lung development, characterized by fewer and enlarged alveoli, fibrosis, and airway inflammation, all of which contribute to long-term respiratory difficulties.
